title: chore(deps): resolve @objectstack/* 17.6.0 in pnpm-lock.yaml and follow its mechanical contract moves; five owner-held reds reported by row (objectui#11438)
body:
Fixes #11438

## What this PR is

`pnpm-lock.yaml` now resolves `@objectstack/*` 17.6.0, regenerated with pnpm only and never edited by hand. Every gate that the bump turned red is listed below by row. The mechanical ones are done on this branch. The rest are still red, each owned by a card that is on hold waiting for this very bump, plus one with no owner. Those rows are why this PR is a draft that needs a seat decision; see "Still red" below.

| package | before (`main` lock) | after |
|---|---|---|
| `@objectstack/spec` · `types` · `core` · `client` · `formula` · `lint` · `sdui-parser` | 17.5.0 | 17.6.0 |

Nothing else moved. The resolution census compares package and snapshot keys between `origin/main`'s lock and this branch's lock in both directions: seven keys removed at 17.5.0 and seven added at 17.6.0, with no importer `specifier` line changed. The 17.6.0 packages ask for `zod ^4.6.5`, which the lock already resolves.

**How the lock was regenerated.** I used the 17.5.0 bump's route (objectui#11073). Every `@objectstack/*` specifier was raised to `^17.6.0` for one `pnpm install`. Every manifest was then restored byte for byte to HEAD, and a second `pnpm install` reconciled the importers back to their declared ranges. objectui#11509 (the jsdom 29.1 pin) landed on `main` while this was in flight. I merged `main` as a merge commit, not a rebase. git merged the lockfile without a conflict. Then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` exited 0 with engine-strict on, a plain `pnpm install` left the lockfile byte-identical, and the census against the new `main` lock shows only the seven `@objectstack/*` moves.

## B3: lockfile-only, or must every floor move?

Lockfile-only, plus whatever floors the floor gates demand. Today they demand none, so no `package.json` changes.

- `check:spec-floors` (`scripts/check-spec-range-floors.mjs`): its header says "A package's declared `@objectstack/spec` FLOOR must carry every symbol that package's own published artifact references". It judges symbol presence only. Over a full build it printed: "✅ Every consumer-facing @objectstack/spec floor carries the symbols its package's artifact references". With `--cross-check` it also printed "Dual-package cross-check: 54 entry point(s) — the `import` and `require` halves export the same names". Both exited 0.
- `check:installed-pin-claims` judges prose about the installed version, never a declared range. Its findings were 38 prose sites, handled below.
- No other rule here asks for floors to track the newest release. objectui#5793's ruling is "floors track reality", which the floor gate enforces. Every declared range already admits 17.6.0. No package in this PR imports a 17.6.0-only export from published code; the one 17.6.0-only import (`@objectstack/spec/migrations`) is in a test file. So the consuming cards raise their own floors when they first import such an export.

## Disposition by row

### Done here (mechanical)

| gate / test | what 17.6.0 moved | done here |
|---|---|---|
| `check:spec-symbols` | `@objectstack/spec/ui` now exports `EmptyState`, the authoring type of a list view's empty-state config | ALLOW entry for `@object-ui/components:EmptyState`, which is a React component alias. That is the same disposition objectui#11073 gave the four `Object*Props` collisions. |
| `check:installed-pin-claims` | 38 sites named 17.5.0 | Each fact was re-measured on 17.6.0 with a 17.5.0 tarball as the control, then restamped. The retired-key spelling moved (see next row) and was reworded. Seven sites in four files that name a past release were added to the ledger as `historical`. Gate: `OK`. |
| retired-key pins (`retired-key-type.ts` and five pins) | the pinned spec's tombstone type is now the branded `[REMOVED]` mark, as on `main` | reworded: "the branded mark at the pinned 17.6.0 and on objectstack `main`, bare `undefined` through 17.5.0" |
| `writeWarningToast.test.ts` tripwire | `DroppedFieldsEventSchema.reason` lists `computed` | Did what the tripwire asked: the `\| 'computed'` widening is gone, the spent tripwire is deleted, and `_ReasonIsTheEnum` pins the exact four-member union |
| `DatasetWidget.unrenderedMeasures-8894` | the root no longer exports `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR` (migrations-entry-split) | static import from `@objectstack/spec/migrations`, as its docblock asked |
| registry parity: "page:header declares no top-level input the spec does not accept" | `PageHeaderProps.breadcrumb` is a tombstone (objectstack#20758) | The `page:header` registration drops its `breadcrumb` input, which the renderer has not read since objectui#11166; the entry's own comment said it would leave with the retirement. The slotted-pages guide example drops `breadcrumb: true`, and the page-header doc now says the key is refused. |
| registry parity: dangling exemptions and ledger caps | `action:button` and `action:icon` no longer declare `endpoint` (objectstack `b3917d90`) | The two stale objectui#11111 bookings are struck. The cap goes from 3 to 1 and the owner total from 3 to 1; `undoable` is still owed to objectui#11168. |
| `loadLanguage.test.tsx` | the served translations gain a `picklists` group (objectstack `addbbf02`) | `@object-ui/i18n` recognises the group |
| `MetadataFieldsPage.refusalIssues-11302` | the `constructor` field-name refusal is raised at its key (objectstack#20997) | the reading moves to `custom @ fields.constructor`, which the pin said is the only change needed |
| `MetadataService.retiredObjectEnabled` / `.specKeyObjectPayload` | `ObjectSchema` gains `imageField` (43 to 44 keys; lost set empty) | corpus-guard count re-pointed, the same way the 17.3.0 adoption was |
| `vite-objectstack-spec-dist.test.ts` | the exports map gains `./migrations` (20 to 21; no `browser` arm; nothing removed) | counts and prose re-pinned |
| `check-lockfile-integrity.test.ts` | its samples were keyed on the 17.5.0 snapshot keys | samples rebuilt on the 17.6.0 keys, as its own tripwire asked |
| `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` | the live-e2e backend pin must equal the resolved spec | `OBJECTSTACK_VERSION=17.6.0` (`@objectstack/cli@17.6.0` resolves to the 17.6.0 tag commit) |
| `grouping-field-padded-refused-7347` | `object-grid.grouping` is typed (it was `unknown`) | the bag member now refuses a padded name on every face, so it moves from the uncovered table to the declaring table; the node-level flat refusal stays uncovered |
| `nested-page-children-11223` | the spec's walk descends `page:card`'s `properties.footer[]` | The footer becomes a row of (a) and block (e) retires itself as it instructed. The CLI doc no longer names the footer as unjudged. ⚠️ Block (e) also asks that the close be recorded on objectui#11223. That is a card write outside this dispatch's budget, so it is left to the seat. |
| `check:eager-closure` (Bundle Analysis) | the spec root sheds its migration chain: −250,096 gzipped eager bytes | The ceilings come down by exactly what was recovered (the second payback, objectstack#20646): aggregate 3,660,380 to 3,410,284, and `vendor-objectstack` 1,689,265 to 1,439,157. The baselines move to `2ba091c`. Two console builds were taken in one lock hold, with `main` `2d576e46` as the control; the table is in the file. Left unchanged, the gauge was blind (exit 2, headroom 3.01x). |

### Still red: not mechanical, reported by row

Every row below is owned by a card that is `pm:on-hold` until objectui resolves 17.6.0, which is this PR. So it is circular: the bump cannot land green without the owner's work, and the owner waits for the bump. Each row gives the gate, the failing assertion, and the 17.6.0 commit or row that moved it.

1. **`object-grid` declares `description`, `emptyState`, `keyboardNavigation`** (objectstack `f5c7b2c7`, #20882). Owner: objectui#11227 (held), with objectui#11068.
   - `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` "object-grid publishes every top-level key its spec props schema declares": `['description', 'emptyState', 'keyboardNavigation']` unpublished.
   - Same file, "the four GA blocks resolve their ruled split": objectui#4648's split forbids standing an exemption in for a declaration on a GA block, so booking these three keys is not available without a ruling.
   - `object-grid-properties-bag-11276.test.ts`, 4 rows ("the row does not declare emptyState / keyboardNavigation …"): the recorded spec readings flipped.
2. **`record:line_items` gets its `ComponentPropsMap` row** (objectstack `24c554da`, #21142 / #21244). Owner: objectui#11536. **Booked on this branch** (`00c13e7`, `c9121f9`) under ruling A′ (record 5965062249), which applies objectui#11111 decision 3 = B.
   - `record:line_items` joins `EXPECTED_COVERED` as `MINOR_17_6_BLOCKS`, and the census reads 56 carried / 40 judged.
   - The ten unpublished keys and the two unpinned members (`columns`, `dataSource`) are ledgered OWED TO objectui#11536, with "Expires 2026-11-02, or when objectui#11536 lands".
   - The caps move: `unpublishedKeys` 1 to 11, `memberPins` 0 to 2, `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTION_CEILING` 0 to 2.
   - Nothing is declared or pinned. All of row 2's assertions are green.
3. **The dimensionless measure-arity check** (`checkDashboardWidgetDimensionlessMeasureArity`; objectstack `11d28c17`, #21053; objectui#8894 ruling D). Owner: objectui#11334 (held).
   - `spec-object-refinements-7715.test.ts` (2): the spec object now carries 3 object-level checks, and objectui's mirror re-attaches 2.
   - `dashboard-widget-metric-measure-door-8894.test.ts` (14) and `WidgetConfigPanel.measureDoor-8894.test.tsx` (21): a dimensionless `pie` / `donut` / `funnel` / `scatter` / `treemap` / `sankey` / `radar` with two measures is refused by the spec and accepted by objectui's door.
   - ⚠️ Not a one-line attach. objectstack `main` already renamed the export to `checkDashboardWidgetChartMeasureArity` (`32d57690`, #21293 / #21425, after 17.6.0) and no longer exports the 17.6.0 name. A static import would compile on the pin and fail the Spec Main Shape Gate. I attached it, measured that, and reverted.
4. **`$empty` joins `FILTER_OPERATORS`, and `is_empty` / `is_not_empty` lower to it** (objectstack `f1e921ab`, #20446 / #20570). Owner: objectui#11094 (held), and objectui#10813.
   - ⚠️ A runtime regression if this lands alone. `ValueDataSource.astFilterVocabulary.test.ts` (6): an `is_empty` / `is_not_empty` rule selects nothing in `ValueDataSource`, because the lowering now emits `$empty` and the matcher does not execute it.
   - `filter-source-merge.test.ts` (1): `{ $empty: true }` where `{ $null: true }` was expected.
   - `ValueDataSource.dollarFilterVocabulary.test.ts`, `ValueDataSource.filterLogicConformance-8513.test.ts`, `FilterConditionField.operators.test.ts`, `readme-filter-operator-table.test.ts` (1 each): the staged-`$empty` tripwires.
5. **`ActionSchema` gains `outcomeMessages`** (objectstack `d6d6e872`, #21214). Owner: objectui#11344 (held).
   - `actionKeys.pin.test.ts` "lists every key the spec ActionSchema declares": `outcomeMessages` is missing from the inventory.

The full-suite reading on the merged head is in the test section below. ⛔ None of these assertions was weakened, and no hold was touched.

## Tests

On the merged head `40d9b5a`, the whole suite ran with the repository-root form `pnpm exec vitest run` under the verify lock:

    Test Files  12 failed | 4318 passed | 7 skipped (4337)
         Tests  60 failed | 58922 passed | 356 skipped (59338)

All 60 failures are the five families under "Still red": 7 + 21 + 14 + 2 rows from families 1 to 3, 6 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 rows from family 4, and 1 row from family 5. No other test failed. `turbo run type-check` ran 81/81 tasks on the same head. On the lockfile-only commit `3796d59`, the bump-caused reds also included every mechanical row in the table above. Each of those rows is green here.

The `main` that this branch merged had moved by one more commit before this PR opened (`6903eaf`, objectui#11523, docs only). The merge queue rebuilds on it.

## Changeset

`.changeset/11438-objectstack-17-6-bump.md`: `@object-ui/components`, `@object-ui/i18n` and `@object-ui/console`, all `patch`, no `major`. The other `src/` edits are comment restamps or a type-only change with no runtime effect.

- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: "✅  33 source file(s) of 14 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s): .changeset/11438-objectstack-17-6-bump.md." (exit 0)
- `check-changeset-no-major`: exit 0.
- `check:changeset-claims` exits 0. It is report-only, and it asks for a read of 59 pending changesets that name a file this branch edits. This branch's edits to those files are restamped comments, a test re-pin, or the `breadcrumb` input. None of them changes a fact those changesets state.

## Size and route

726 changed lines (414 additions, 312 deletions) across 46 files against the merge base `8366acc`, lockfile included, which is under the 5,000-line human-merge line. `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` reports every path NOT GOVERNED. Clause ②: no.

## Acceptance notes (observations, not filed)

- `packages/types/src/objectql.ts`, the `ObjectCalendarSchema.data` docblock: the sentence "`object-map` and `object-gantt` have no `ComponentPropsMap` row at all" was already false at 17.5.0. Both rows exist at 17.5.0 and at 17.6.0. I restamped only the measured line beside it.
- `retired-key-type.ts`: the bare-`undefined` arm now describes no installed spec, so it can be dropped. That tightens a helper every retirement pin reads, so I kept it here.
- `@object-ui/i18n` now namespaces a `picklists` group under `app`. Nothing in objectui reads `app.picklists` yet; that is the picklist feature's work (objectui#10202, held), not this bump's.
- `BASELINE.squashMerge` in `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` stays `null` and is owed a back-fill once this lands, the same as after objectui#11101.

## Deviation

The container runs Node 22.22.0. Before objectui#11509 reached this branch, the root `jsdom ^30.0.1` required `^22.22.2`, and `.npmrc`'s `engine-strict=true` refused every install. Until the merge, local installs ran with `--config.engine-strict=false`. That flag turns an engine refusal into a warning and does not change resolution: pnpm passes `engineStrict` only to the installability check, not to the resolver. After the merge, every install and gate above runs with engine-strict on.
